business_model.claim: American Tower Corporation is a United States real estate investment trust in the REIT - Specialty industry that owns, operates, and develops multitenant communications real estate.
quotes: industry: REIT - Specialty
We are one of the largest global real estate investment trusts and a leading independent owner, operator and developer of multitenant communications real estate.

business_model.claim: As a U.S. federal income tax REIT, American Tower generally does not pay U.S. federal income taxes on REIT-qualified income due to the dividends paid deduction, while paying U.S. federal income taxes on domestic taxable REIT subsidiaries and local taxes on international operations.
quotes: Accordingly, we generally are not required to pay U.S. federal income taxes on income generated by our REIT operations, including the income derived from leasing space on our towers and in our data centers, as we receive a dividends paid deduction for distributions to stockholders that offsets our REIT taxable income and gains.
However, we remain obligated to pay U.S. federal income taxes on earnings from our domestic taxable REIT subsidiaries (“TRSs”).

business_model.claim: The company's primary business is property operations—leasing space on communications sites and U.S. data centers—which accounted for 97% of total revenues in 2025 and 98% of total revenues in the nine months ended September 30, 2026.
quotes: We refer to this business, inclusive of our data center business discussed below, as our property operations, which accounted for 97% of our total revenues for the year ended December 31, 2025.

We refer to the business encompassing the above as our property operations, which accounted for 98% and 98% of our total revenues for the three and nine months ended September 30, 2026, respectively, and includes our U.S. & Canada property, Africa & Asia-Pacific (“APAC”) property, Europe property and Latin America property segments and Data Centers segment.

business_model.claim: As of September 30, 2026, the communications real estate portfolio (excluding managed sites) included 130,787 owned towers, 15,735 operated towers, and 847 owned DAS sites across the U.S. & Canada, Africa & APAC, Europe, and Latin America, alongside managed rooftop and tower sites, fiber assets, property interests, and shared backup power solutions.
quotes: In addition to the communications sites in our portfolio, we manage rooftop and tower sites for property owners under various contractual arrangements.

business_model.claim: American Tower also sells U.S. tower-related services—site application, zoning and permitting, structural and mount analyses, construction management, and program management—which primarily support its site leasing business and generated 339.6 (table in millions) of revenue in 2025 and 180.3 (table in millions) in the nine months ended September 30, 2026.
quotes: These services include site application, zoning and permitting, structural and mount analyses, and construction management services, together with program management offerings that support customer deployment needs from project scoping through construction.
Our services operations primarily support our site leasing business, including the addition of new tenants and equipment on our sites.

business_model.claim: Its customer base consists of wireless service providers, radio and television broadcast companies, wireless data providers, government agencies, and municipalities on communications sites; enterprises, network operators, cloud providers, and supporting service providers in data centers; and communications service providers and third-party tower operators for fiber and property interests.
quotes: Our primary business is the leasing of space on communications sites to wireless service providers, radio and television broadcast companies, wireless data providers, government agencies and municipalities and tenants in a number of other industries.

We also hold other telecommunications infrastructure, fiber and property interests that we lease primarily to communications service providers and third-party tower operators, and, as discussed further below, we hold a portfolio of highly interconnected data center facilities and related assets in the United States that we provide for the leasing of space primarily to enterprises, network operators, cloud providers and supporting service providers.

business_model.claim: Revenue is concentrated in a small number of customers: in 2025, T-Mobile (18%), AT&T (17%), Verizon Wireless (14%), and Telefónica (10%) each represented at least 10% of total revenues, while top customers accounted for 85% of U.S. & Canada, 81% of Africa & APAC, 70% of Europe, and 71% of Latin America property segment revenue.
quotes: A substantial portion of our total operating revenues is derived from a small number of customers.
U.S. & Canada: AT&T Inc. (“AT&T”); T-Mobile US, Inc. (“T-Mobile”); and Verizon Communications Inc. (“Verizon Wireless”) accounted for an aggregate of 85% of U.S. & Canada property segment revenue.

business_model.claim: American Tower reports across U.S. & Canada property (49% of 2025 total revenue; $5,248.7 in table in millions), Africa & APAC property (13%; 1,422.9 in table in millions), Europe property (9%; 937.7 in table in millions), Latin America property (15%; 1,642.6 in table in millions), Data Centers (10%; 1,053.1 in table in millions), and Services (3%; 339.6 in table in millions), out of $10,644.6 (table in millions) total 2025 revenue.
quotes: We report our results in six segments: U.S. & Canada property (which includes all assets in the United States and Canada, other than our data center facilities and related assets), Africa & Asia-Pacific (“APAC”) property, Europe property, Latin America property, Data Centers and Services.

business_model.basis: stated in P3, P4, and P5
business_model.claim: The company has narrowed its geographic footprint through divestitures, selling South Africa fiber in 2025, ATC Philippines and its controlling interest in Kirtonkhola Tower Bangladesh Limited in June 2026, and agreeing to sell its Canada operations for approximately 288 million Canadian Dollars (approximately $202 million).
quotes: During the year ended December 31, 2025, we completed the sale of our fiber assets in South Africa (“South Africa Fiber”).
Sale of Philippines Subsidiary—On June 15, 2026, we completed the sale of ATC Philippines.

Divestitures – During the three months ended September 30, 2026, the Company, through its subsidiary, American Towers LLC, entered into an agreement pursuant to which it expects to sell 100% of the ownership interests in its subsidiaries in Canada for total aggregate consideration of approximately 288 million Canadian Dollars (approximately $202 million).

business_model.basis: stated in P1, P3, and P4
business_model.claim: Tenant leases for communications sites generally have initial non-cancellable multiyear terms with multiple renewal options and periodic escalations—averaging approximately 3% fixed annually in the United States or tied to inflation in most international markets—underpinning nearly $49 billion of expected future non-cancellable customer lease revenue as of September 30, 2026 (down from over $54 billion as of December 31, 2025).
quotes: In most of our markets, our tenant leases for our communications sites with wireless carriers generally have initial non-cancellable terms of five to ten years with multiple renewal terms.

Most of our tenant leases for our communications sites have provisions that periodically increase or “escalate” the rent due under the lease, typically based on (a) an annual fixed escalation (averaging approximately 3% in the United States), (b) an inflationary index in most of our international markets, or (c) a combination of both.

Based upon existing customer leases and foreign currency exchange rates as of September 30, 2026, we expect to generate nearly $49 billion of non-cancellable customer lease revenue over future periods, before the impact of straight-line lease accounting.

business_model.claim: Property revenue grows from adding tenants (colocations) and equipment amendments on existing sites, contractual escalations net of churn, acquiring or building new sites (approximately 2,230 sites added globally in 2025), and data center lease commencements, expansions, mark-to-market renewals, and interconnections (with Data Centers cash revenue up 16.3% and Organic Tenant Billings Growth at 1.1% in the third quarter of 2026).
quotes: During the year ended December 31, 2025, we grew our portfolio of communications real estate through the acquisition and construction of approximately 2,230 communications sites globally.
Total property revenue increased 4.5% to $2,734 million, driven by 1.1% Organic Tenant Billings Growth and 16.3% cash revenue growth in Data Centers(1)

business_model.basis: stated in P2, P3, and P4
business_model.claim: Property revenue is pressured by churn—which rose from approximately 2% of tenant billings in 2025 to approximately 5% in the nine months ended September 30, 2026 after 100% of DISH revenue (2% of 2025 total property revenue) was reflected in churn following its default and bankruptcy filing—and by reserves of approximately $30 million in 2025 and approximately $30 million in the nine months ended September 30, 2026 from an arbitration dispute with AT&T Mexico ($300 million of 2025 tenant revenue).
quotes: During the nine months ended September 30, 2026, churn was approximately 5% of our tenant billings, primarily driven by churn due to one of our U.S. customers, DISH Wireless L.L.C., a subsidiary of DISH Network Corporation (“DISH”) in our U.S. & Canada property segment, as discussed below.
Beginning on January 1, 2026, 100% of DISH revenue has been reflected in churn.

We incurred approximately $30 million of reserves during the year ended December 31, 2025, and approximately $30 million of additional reserves during the nine months ended September 30, 2026, related to this customer.

business_model.claim: Reported revenue is also moved by international pass-through reimbursements for ground rent, power, and fuel (which vary with fuel prices), foreign currency exchange fluctuations across Latin America, Africa & APAC, and Europe, and non-cash straight-line revenue recognition (which was approximately $(24.0) million in the third quarter of 2026 versus approximately $27.7 million in the prior-year period).
quotes: A portion of the Company’s pass-through revenue is based on power and fuel expense reimbursements and therefore subject to fluctuations in fuel prices.
The majority of the Company’s Latin America, Africa & APAC and Europe revenue and operating expenses are denominated in each country’s local currency.

Q3 2026 growth rates impacted by a decrease in non-cash straight-line revenue, which represented approximately $(24.0) million in the current period as compared to approximately $27.7 million in the prior-year period.

business_model.basis: stated in F2, P1, and P3
business_model.claim: Direct property costs of operations (2,097.6 in table in millions for the nine months ended September 30, 2026, compared to 1,897.2 in the prior-year period) consist primarily of ground rent—largely fixed under long-term leases with annual escalations—power and fuel costs, property taxes, and repairs and maintenance, with ground rent or power and fuel costs partly or wholly passed through to tenants in many international markets.
quotes: Our costs typically include ground rent (which is primarily fixed under long-term lease agreements with annual cost escalations) and power and fuel costs, some or all of which may be passed through to our tenants, as well as property taxes and repair and maintenance expenses.

Direct operating expenses incurred by our property segments include direct site or facility level expenses and consist primarily of ground rent and power and fuel costs, some or all of which may be passed through to our customers, as well as property taxes and repairs and maintenance expenses.

business_model.basis: stated in F2, P1, P3, and P5
business_model.claim: Adding new tenants or equipment on existing sites requires minimal incremental direct cost and little additional property SG&A, yielding high operating margins (Property Gross Margin % was 73.5% in the third quarter of 2026), while consolidated selling, general, administrative and development expense was 719.4 (table in millions) in the nine months ended September 30, 2026.
quotes: Incremental operating costs associated with adding new tenants or equipment to an existing communications site are typically relatively minimal.

In general, our property segments’ selling, general, administrative and development expenses do not significantly increase as a result of adding incremental customers to our sites or facilities and typically increase only modestly year-over-year.

business_model.basis: stated in F2, P1, and P5
business_model.claim: Maintaining communications sites requires relatively low capital expenditures (170 to 180 for capital improvements and 15 for corporate in the full-year 2026 outlook, table in millions), whereas total capex is driven by discretionary site builds and data center development (full-year 2026 total capex outlook of $1,765 to $1,875 in table in millions, including $695 million for Data Centers), alongside 1,552.0 (table in millions) of depreciation, amortization and accretion in the nine months ended September 30, 2026.
quotes: On average, we require relatively low amounts of annual capital expenditures to maintain our communications sites.
During the third quarter of 2026, total capital expenditures were approximately $407 million, of which $48 million was for non-discretionary capital improvements and corporate capital expenditures.

quotes: We have a substantial amount of indebtedness.

competitive_position.claim: Direct competition from peers offering alternative communications infrastructure and competing pricing or contractual terms threatens lease rates and renewals, while larger or less return-disciplined rivals compete to build or acquire new assets.
quotes: Our industries are highly competitive and our customers have numerous alternatives in leasing communications infrastructure assets.

Some of our competitors are larger and may have greater financial resources than we do, while other competitors may apply less stringent investment criteria or less stringent contractual terms than we have.

competitive_position.basis: Stated in the 2025 Form 10-K Item 1A Risk Factors.
competitive_position.claim: In data centers, some competitors hold advantages in scale, brand, leverage, network access, and lower power or operating costs, which are compounded by annual expirations of a significant share of American Tower's data center leases.
quotes: In addition, some of our data center competitors may have significant advantages over us, including greater name recognition, longer operating histories, lower operating costs, lower levels of leverage, pre-existing relationships with current or potential customers, greater financial, marketing and other resources, access to better networks and access to less expensive power.
These risks are compounded by the fact that a significant percentage of our data center customer leases expire every year.

competitive_position.basis: Stated in the 2025 Form 10-K Item 1A Risk Factors.
competitive_position.claim: Customer consolidation, market exits, and infrastructure sharing—such as RAN sharing, roaming, or resale arrangements—threaten to slow new leasing activity and trigger equipment decommissioning or lease non-renewals.
quotes: Significant consolidation among our customers could reduce demand for our communications infrastructure and may materially and adversely affect our growth and revenues.
Our ongoing contractual revenues and our future results may be negatively impacted if a significant number of these leases are terminated or not renewed.

competitive_position.basis: Stated in the 2025 Form 10-K Item 1A Risk Factors.
competitive_position.claim: New wireless and computing technologies—including spectrally efficient equipment, small cells, satellite services, and power-intensive AI workloads exceeding existing data center power and cooling density—could shift carrier budgets away from towers or render existing facilities obsolete.
quotes: In addition, if the industry trends toward deploying increased capital to the development and implementation of new technologies, then customers may allocate less of their budgets to leasing space on our towers.

Similarly, our data center site infrastructure may become antiquated or obsolete due to the development of new systems that deliver power to, or eliminate heat from, the servers and other customer equipment that we house or due to the development of new technology, such as AI, which is potentially more power-intensive, that requires levels of power and cooling density that our facilities may not be designed to provide.

quotes: We have a substantial amount of indebtedness.

quotes: Our ability to lease additional space on our sites is primarily a function of the rate at which wireless carriers and other tenants deploy capital to improve and expand their wireless networks.

Additionally, certain small cell complementary network technologies or satellite services could shift a portion of our customers’ network investments away from traditional tower-based networks, which may reduce the need for carriers to add more equipment at certain communications sites.

growth_thesis.basis: stated in the Q3 2026 Form 10-Q Item 2 MD&A

quotes: Most of our tenant leases for our communications sites have provisions that periodically increase or “escalate” the rent due under the lease, typically based on (a) an annual fixed escalation (averaging approximately 3% in the United States), (b) an inflationary index in most of our international markets, or a combination of both.

Based upon existing customer leases and foreign currency exchange rates as of September 30, 2026, we expect to generate nearly $49 billion of non-cancellable customer lease revenue over future periods, before the impact of straight-line lease accounting.

growth_thesis.basis: stated in the 2025 Form 10-K Item 1A Risk Factors and Q3 2026 Form 10-Q Item 2 MD&A
growth_thesis.claim: Continued growth from contractual escalations requires high lease renewals without material churn, customer solvency and contract performance, and inflation that does not exceed fixed escalator percentages.
quotes: If any of these customers are unwilling or unable to perform their obligations under their agreements with us, our revenues, results of operations, financial condition and liquidity could be materially and adversely affected.
In addition, should inflation rates exceed our fixed escalator percentages in markets where our leases include fixed escalators, our returns could be adversely affected.

growth_thesis.basis: stated in the 2025 Form 10-K Item 7 MD&A

quotes: We anticipate increasing network densification over the next several years, as existing network density is anticipated to be insufficient to account for rapidly increasing levels of wireless data usage.

Continued spectrum acquisition and deployment by wireless service providers, which is expected to result in additional sites and equipment on existing sites as operators optimize network configuration and utilize the additional spectrum.

growth_thesis.basis: stated in the 2025 Form 10-K Item 1A Risk Factors and Item 7 MD&A
growth_thesis.claim: For mobile data and spectrum trends to translate into revenue growth, wireless carriers must sustain capital deployment and continue outsourcing tower infrastructure rather than shifting budgets to alternative network architectures.
quotes: According to industry data, recent aggregate annual wireless capital spending in the United States has averaged at least $30 billion, resulting in consistent demand for our sites.
Further, a customer may decide to cease outsourcing tower infrastructure or otherwise change its business model, which would result in a decrease in our revenue and operating results.

growth_thesis.basis: stated in the 2025 Form 10-K Item 7 MD&A and Q3 2026 Form 8-K earnings release
growth_thesis.claim: The U.S. Data Centers segment is a primary growth driver, delivering 16.3% cash revenue growth in the third quarter of 2026 and full-year 2026 revenue outlook growth of 16.1% at the midpoint, supported by hybrid-cloud, multi-cloud, interconnection, and early-stage AI workloads.
quotes: As a result of Data Centers segment outperformance, the Company is raising the midpoint of its full year 2026 outlook for property revenue by $55 million.

Our portfolio of highly interconnected data center facilities and related assets in the United States is well positioned to monetize elevated demand for hybrid-cloud and multi-cloud deployments, as well as demand from early-stage AI-related workloads like inferencing, machine learning models and GPU-as-a-Service from neo clouds.

growth_thesis.basis: stated in the 2025 Form 10-K Item 1A Risk Factors

quotes: Similarly, our data center site infrastructure may become antiquated or obsolete due to the development of new systems that deliver power to, or eliminate heat from, the servers and other customer equipment that we house or due to the development of new technology, such as AI, which is potentially more power-intensive, that requires levels of power and cooling density that our facilities may not be designed to provide.
These risks are compounded by the fact that a significant percentage of our data center customer leases expire every year.

growth_thesis.basis: stated in the 2025 Form 10-K Item 7 MD&A and Q3 2026 Form 8-K earnings release

quotes: In addition, we intend to continue to supplement our organic growth by selectively developing or acquiring new sites in our existing and new markets where we can achieve our risk-adjusted return on investment objectives.

We believe that the network technology migration we have seen in the United States, which has led to significantly denser networks and meaningful new business commencements for us over a number of years, will be replicated in our international markets over time.

growth_thesis.basis: stated in the 2025 Form 10-K Item 1A Risk Factors and Q3 2026 Form 8-K earnings release
